description:
Round-28 perf lever L6 (docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md §A.2 row 5).

=== DONE (s470bp) ===

`@a = (1..$n)` and `@a = (1..20, $_)` are how Perl builds an array, and both
went through the general path: `p-..` allocated a simple-vector of the whole
range, the enclosing `(vector …)` allocated another, `%p-snapshot-array-rhs`
walked it, and only then were the elements pushed into the destination.  The
destination's elements ARE the counting loop.

THE LICENCE IS SYNTACTIC and it is `p-array-=`'s own view of its VALUE form
(`%p-fill-segments`): a bare `(p-.. A B)`, or a literal `(vector S1 … Sk)` at
least one of whose pieces is one.  REQUIRING a range is the point — without one
the general path is already the better answer, because since task #1181 it has
the block copy, and this must not steal its work.

WHAT THE SEGMENT PATH STILL DOES, in this order, because perl does:
  * evaluate every piece — the range BOUNDS included — before the destination
    is cleared, and SNAPSHOT each non-range piece, so `@a = (1..2, @a)` still
    reads the old @a (probed: `1 2 1 2`);
  * run the whole-array-assignment checks and reset the each() iterator
    (%p-array-fill-start — the three things p-array-fill does before its walk);
  * store each non-range piece through the SAME walk the general path uses:
    `%p-array-add-items`, which was EXTRACTED from p-array-fill (it was the
    `add-items` LABELS) rather than copied, so flattening, holes and boxing
    stay one rule;
  * refuse an oversized range with perl's own two messages —
    `%p-range-size-check`, also extracted, shared with `p-..`;
  * store elements through the RAW-ELEMENT GATE: a range's elements are plain
    integers, for which %p-array-store-scalar stores raw when *p-raw-elems* is
    on and a BOX when it is off, so the direct arm is taken only while the gate
    is on.  A fast path must disappear with the gate or the all-boxed A/B world
    stops being measurable.
A magical STRING range ('a'..'zz') has no counting form: that segment goes
through `p-..` and the ordinary walk — the same call the general path makes.

NO PCL_OPT NAME, for task #1181's reason: a runtime macro, no emission to
switch.  Guard rows are macroexpansions with negatives.

MEASURED.  Hand-replaced A/B first: `arrfill` **-93.9 %** against a control
pair at -1.0 %.  SHIPPED, two-core runtime A/B against a `027ba9c` runtime:
**arrfill -58.3 % / -58.0 %** (1.47x -> 0.61x of perl, i.e. from slower than
perl to well under it), best-of-5 and best-of-7.

BARS: gate 210 files (only the 13 pclxs xs rows); nine array-fill probe shapes
vs perl 5.40.3 identical; guard `Pl/t/perf-levers-02.t`, inverse-verified.
subject: L6/#1204 SHIPPED (s470bp): an array assignment from a RANGE is not materialised — arrfill -58.3 % shipped (-93.9 % hand-replaced), 1.47x -> 0.61x of perl
